chapterNote: The shortest chapter in the Bible — two verses, some seventeen Hebrew words by the usual count — and by the traditional chapter count its middle chapter, the hinge the whole book swings on. It is a summons to every nation and every people-group to praise the LORD, and it gives one reason: His covenant love has prevailed mightily over us, and His faithfulness is forever. The 'us' is Israel; the 'you' is the whole world — the nations invited to praise God for what He did for someone else, because what He did for Israel was always aimed at them. Paul saw it and quoted it in Romans 15 as one of his proof-texts that the Gentiles were in the plan from the beginning. Great truths do not always need many words.

1.text: Praise the LORD, all you nations! Sing His praise, all you peoples!
1.amp: O praise [halal] the LORD [YHWH], all ye nations [goy]: praise [shabach — laud, commend] Him, all ye people [ummah — peoples, tribes].
1.notes: Short as it is, no psalm casts a wider net: kol goyim, kol ha-ummim (H1471, H523) — every nation and every ethnic community summoned by two praise-verbs, halal and shabach (H1984, H7623). Paul quotes it as proof that the Gentiles were always meant to worship Israel's God (cf. Romans 15:11).

2.text: For His covenant love has prevailed mightily over us, and the faithfulness of the LORD endures forever. Praise the LORD!
2.amp: For His merciful kindness [chesed — covenant love] is great [gabar — has prevailed, been mighty] toward us: and the truth [emeth — faithfulness] of the LORD [YHWH] endures for ever [olam]. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
2.notes: gabar (H1396) is the warrior-verb, 'to prevail': chesed (H2617) does not merely exist toward us; it overpowers us — grace as a conquering force. And emeth (H571) le-olam (H5769), faithfulness forever: chesed and emeth are the pair the LORD named of Himself at Sinai (cf. Exodus 34:6) — one mighty, one permanent. A handful of Hebrew words, and the whole gospel's shape.
